title: Introduce interaction slate fabricator and sparse metric aggregator for slate-based workload synthesis
author: Priya Menon
description:
Motivation: We need a lightweight, deterministic runner to synthesize compact 'interaction slates' — short multi-turn groups of related requests that appear together in product traffic (e.g., user search + follow-up clarification + inline embed request). Existing runners focus on long-session replayers or single-turn bursts; they do not model correlated intra-slate semantics nor emit sparse, attribution-friendly metrics for kernel/kv/cache contributions. This PR adds the `slate-fabricator` workload generator and a companion `sparse-metric-aggregator` telemetry exporter.

Design summary: single binary (benchtool/slate_fabricator) that composes slates from small building blocks: intents, short dialogues, and auxiliary calls (embeddings/rerank). Slates are parameterized by: slate size distribution (1-5 interactions), inter-interaction spacing distribution (0-500ms), and dependency graphs (which interactions re-use KV prefixes). The fabricator supports deterministic seeding and a compact serialized "slate manifest" for exact replayability across runs. The sparse-metric-aggregator collects attribution tuples at the per-interaction granularity (slate_id, interaction_idx, kernel_hint, kvcache_hit_ratio, token_counts) and exports compact line-protocol JSON to S3/MinIO for downstream correlation with perf traces.

What changed (high-level):
- New runner: benchtool/slate_fabricator with CLI flags for slate profiles, seeding, rate/pacing, and epoch durations.
- New telemetry plugin: telemetry/sparse_aggregator that subscribes to the runner's internal event bus and collapses metrics into sparse vectors (only non-zero dimensions) to reduce telemetry cardinality.
- Integration harness: examples/slate_profiles/{news_search,doc_edit,qa_with_embed}.yaml and CI perf scenario definitions (ci/perf/slate_smoke.yaml).
- Small runtime helpers: runtime/kv_primer.go (deterministic prefix generator) and benchtool/common/slate_serializer.go for manifest format.

Commit summary: 3 commits (described below).

Files changed (high-level): benchtool/slate_fabricator/main.go, benchtool/slate_fabricator/runner.go, benchtool/common/slate_serializer.go, telemetry/sparse_aggregator/aggregator.go, telemetry/sparse_aggregator/exporter_s3.go, examples/slate_profiles/news_search.yaml, examples/slate_profiles/qa_with_embed.yaml, ci/perf/slate_smoke.yaml, runtime/kv_primer.go, README-bench-slate.md, go.mod, go.sum.

Testing and CI: unit tests for slate serialization and sparse aggregator dedup were added under benchtool/.../slate_test.go and telemetry/.../aggregator_test.go. The perf CI job (ci/perf/slate_smoke.yaml) runs a 2-minute synthetic epoch at very low RPS to validate stability and output format. The first CI run showed a perf/regression-check failure due to an expensive metadata aggregation path; I optimized the aggregator's bucket mapping in the second commit and the checks passed.

Backward compatibility: slate manifest format is versioned (v1); new code will fall back to single-interaction generation when given legacy simple inputs. No runtime behavior changes to the main serving code — this lives only in the benchmark-lab tooling and telemetry.

How to run locally (example): `benchtool/slate_fabricator --profile examples/slate_profiles/news_search.yaml --seed 42 --duration 60s --rps 10 --emit-telemetry tcp://localhost:12345` — aggregator can be pointed at the event bus or run in-process with `--embed-aggregator`.

Checklist: 
- [x] Bench runner implemented with deterministic manifest export/import
- [x] Sparse aggregator with S3 exporter and unit tests
- [x] Perf CI scenario and lightweight smoke test
- [x] README with quickstart and minimal examples

Related work items: ENG-6725 (slate workload specification), ENG-6751 (telemetry budget/cost reduction effort).

review_comments: Ethan: Please add a short doc blurb that explains when to use 'slate' vs session replayer. Priya: added README-bench-slate.md with guidance.
Laila: The aggregator creates many small S3 objects at high RPS — can we batch? Priya: added a batching window and configurable shard key in exporter_s3.go; re-ran perf CI.

release_notes: Introduce slate-based synthetic runner and sparse telemetry aggregator for low-cardinality, high-signal benchmarking of correlated short interactions. Useful for modelling product flows composed of 2-5 related calls; includes S3 exporter and CI perf job.
